overview: Teck Resources is a Vancouver-based Canadian diversified base-metals miner that, after exiting steelmaking coal (Elk Valley Resources, sold to Glencore and a Nippon Steel/POSCO consortium for roughly US$8.6 billion, completed July 2024), is now a pure-play copper and zinc 'energy transition metals' producer. It owns or holds interests in five operating mines and a large metallurgical complex across Canada, Chile and Peru, anchored by the Quebrada Blanca (QB2) copper mine in Chile, which is in a multi-year production ramp-up. Teck is in the process of a transformative all-share 'merger of equals' with Anglo American plc (announced September 9, 2025) to form Anglo Teck plc, a top-five global copper producer; the deal has cleared shareholder votes and Canadian ICA approval but remains subject to other international regulatory approvals as of October 2026.

business_model.summary: Teck mines and sells copper and zinc concentrates/refined metal plus by-products (silver, lead, molybdenum, germanium, gold) under commodity-linked pricing. Revenue is transactional/commodity-price-driven rather than recurring, with most concentrate sales priced off LME quotes at the time of shipment and subject to provisional pricing adjustments. Copper has become the dominant revenue and margin driver post-coal-divestiture, with zinc (led by Red Dog and the Trail smelter/refinery) as the second segment.

revenue_streams.name: Copper (QB2, Highland Valley, Antamina 22.5%, Carmen de Andacollo)
Zinc (Red Dog, Trail Operations, Antamina zinc co-product)
By-products (silver, lead, molybdenum, germanium, gold)
revenue_streams.note: embedded within copper/zinc segment revenue above, not incremental

business_model.customer_type: B2B — concentrate and refined metal sold to smelters, traders and industrial end users globally, largely under annual offtake/marketing contracts with LME-referenced pricing
business_model.geographic_mix: Mining operations in Chile (QB2, Carmen de Andacollo), Canada (Highland Valley Copper, Trail B.C.), Peru (Antamina, 22.5% interest) and the U.S. (Red Dog, Alaska); revenue is sold globally, with China a major concentrate buyer. Reporting currency is CAD; most revenue and debt are USD-denominated, operating costs are mixed CAD/CLP.

competitive_position.market_position: Top-10 copper producer in the Americas and the world's largest net zinc miner; mid-cap diversified miner that, pending the Anglo American merger, would become part of a top-five global copper producer (Anglo Teck)

moat_factors.description: QB2 and Highland Valley (life extended to 2046 via the sanctioned HVC MLE project) are large, long-duration ore bodies; Antamina and Red Dog are tier-1 assets, though Red Dog is nearing end of mine life
Operations concentrated in Canada, Chile and Peru — stable mining jurisdictions relative to many peers, though Chile/Peru carry permitting, labour and water/drought risk
Trail Operations is one of the world's largest integrated zinc/lead smelter-refineries, giving some control over the zinc value chain and by-product monetization (germanium, gallium, antimony)
Copper net cash unit costs of ~US$2.03/lb in 2025 are mid-pack, not bottom-quartile; QB2 ramp-up costs have kept costs elevated versus design

If completed, adjacency of QB2 and Anglo's Collahuasi mine in Chile could unlock an estimated US$1.4bn/year of underlying EBITDA uplift from shared infrastructure from 2030-2049, plus ~US$800m/year of pre-tax merger synergies

weaknesses: Single-asset concentration risk at QB2 — a large share of growth and investor expectations ride on an asset still proving out reliable throughput and recoveries
Zinc segment is a structurally declining franchise as Red Dog approaches end of mine life (production guided down from 565kt in 2025 to 410-460kt in 2026 and well below that by 2028)

No major near-term new mine beyond QB2/HVC MLE — other growth projects (Zafranal, San Nicolás, NewRange, Galore Creek, Schaft Creek, NuevaUnión) are pre-sanction and partly paused/deprioritized under the Comprehensive Operational Review
Mid-cap scale leaves Teck as a perennial M&A target/partner, as evidenced by the Anglo American merger and prior Glencore interest
Execution track record at QB2 has been uneven (TMF tailings constraints, shiploader outage in 2025) raising questions about project delivery discipline

growth_drivers: QB2 ramp-up maturing — three consecutive quarters of stable production through Q2 2026, with net cash unit costs falling from US$2.45/lb (Q2 2025) to US$1.83/lb (Q2 2026) as the tailings management facility (TMF) sand wedge build progresses toward a 2026 completion

Highland Valley Copper Mine Life Extension (HVC MLE), sanctioned July 2025, extending Canada's largest copper mine from 2028 to 2046 at ~132,000 tonnes/year average production; C$2.1-2.4bn capex through 2028

Anglo American merger of equals — if completed, creates Anglo Teck, a top-five global copper producer with ~US$800m/year of run-rate synergies and potential US$1.4bn/year EBITDA uplift from QB2/Collahuasi integration from 2030
Copper growth optionality held in reserve (Zafranal, San Nicolás, NewRange, Galore Creek, Schaft Creek, NuevaUnión) for sanctioning once QB2 and HVC MLE execution is derisked

Record/near-record copper prices (LME averaged US$4.51/lb in 2025, up 9% YoY, and US$6.05/lb in Q2 2026) amid structurally tight concentrate supply and historically low smelter treatment charges — a secular tailwind from electrification/AI data-center/grid demand

Capital returned and redeployed from the US$8.6bn EVR coal sale (2024) — debt reduction, buybacks, and dividends — leaving Teck with a net cash position and ~C$9-10bn of liquidity to fund growth or absorb commodity cyclicality

Diversification into critical/specialty by-products (germanium, gallium, antimony) at Trail via the July 2026 Strategic Investment Agreement with Canada Growth Fund and Natural Resources Canada's Critical Minerals Accelerator

business.description: Tailings management facility (sand wedge) development has repeatedly constrained throughput (2023-2025); 2026 guidance still embeds incremental downtime, and debottlenecking beyond nameplate has not yet been sanctioned

Zinc-in-concentrate production guided to fall from 565kt (2025) to 410-460kt (2026), 365-415kt (2027) and 275-325kt (2028) as higher-grade ore is depleted; Red Dog MLE options could extend life beyond 2032 but are not yet committed

business.risk: Antamina/Carmen de Andacollo are non-controlled or minority-interest assets
business.description: Antamina is a 22.5%-owned joint venture with BHP, Glencore and Mitsubishi — Teck does not control operating decisions; Carmen de Andacollo (90% owned) is exposed to Chilean drought risk constraining 2027-2028 guidance

The Anglo American merger of equals remains subject to multiple outstanding international regulatory approvals (as of mid-2026, China and South Korea decisions were still pending); timeline guidance is 12-18 months from the September 2025 announcement (i.e., into H1 2027), and a long approval window creates scope for a rival bid (Glencore/BHP speculation) or deal delay/collapse
Heavy reliance on third-party rail, port and shipping; a 2025 shiploader outage at QB2's port facility (repaired January 2026) illustrates single-point-of-failure logistics risk

financial.description: Nearly all revenue is tied to LME copper/zinc spot and by-product prices; FY2024 continuing-operations pre-tax result was a loss while FY2025/FY2026 have benefited from record copper prices — earnings swing heavily with the cycle

financial.risk: QB2 partner advances not captured in headline debt
financial.description: Advances from Quebrada Blanca partners (Sumitomo Metal Mining/Sumitomo Corp, roughly US$3.1bn / C$4.7-5.0bn) sit outside the reported 'total debt' figure used in standard leverage ratios; a reader comparing Teck's leverage to peers using total debt alone will understate true balance-sheet claims ahead of equity, even though these advances are project-level, non-recourse-style financing rather than corporate debt

financial.risk: Large cash tax payments tied to divestiture gains
financial.description: FY2024 cash flow from operations absorbed roughly C$1.8bn of cash income taxes, partly tied to the EVR sale gain and previously deferred Canadian taxes — a reminder that large one-off gains can carry meaningful deferred tax-payment drag in the following year(s)

financial.risk: Negative free cash flow during ramp-up periods
financial.description: FY2025 FCF was -C$583m due to QB2 ramp costs and working-capital outflows, though H1 2026 (FCF of C$1,285m for the half) shows the ramp-up maturing into strong cash generation

Revenue and most debt are USD-denominated while a large share of costs are CAD- and CLP-denominated and results are reported in CAD; FX swings between USD/CAD and USD/CLP affect both revenue translation and cost base

regulatory.description: Anglo Teck requires antitrust/competition clearance across multiple countries (Canada and Australia cleared; China and South Korea outstanding as of early-mid 2026) plus exchange listing approvals (TSX, NYSE, continuing LSE/JSE)

Canadian approval (Dec 2025) came with binding commitments — at least C$4.5bn of Canadian spend within five years and ~C$10bn cumulative over 15 years — creating an ongoing compliance/monitoring obligation post-close

San Nicolás (Mexico) and Zafranal (Peru) both require pending environmental and land-use permit decisions before sanctioning; Zafranal has been moved to asset preservation with reduced near-term spending pending a better business case

FY2025 results included a C$172m after-tax charge for remeasurement of decommissioning/restoration provisions at closed operations — an ongoing, variable long-tail liability typical of a multi-decade mining portfolio (e.g., B.C. legacy sites, Trail historical operations)

macro.description: LME copper averaged a record US$4.51/lb in 2025 and spiked above US$6/lb in Q2 2026; a reversal in AI/data-center-driven demand expectations, a China slowdown, or new supply could compress margins sharply given Teck's operating leverage
China is a dominant buyer of copper concentrate and a swing factor in both copper and zinc refined demand/supply balances; Chinese import/consumption trends materially move realized prices
FY2025 MD&A specifically flags that U.S. tariff policy is redirecting copper trade patterns and promoting regionalization, adding uncertainty to flow patterns and pricing
New multi-year collective bargaining agreements at QB2 (through 2028) and broader labour/energy cost inflation affect unit costs across the portfolio

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Copper market is forecast to move into a modest deficit in 2026 (global refined production +0.8% to 27.7Mt vs. demand +2.1% to 27.9Mt per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence) on structurally tight concentrate supply, record-low smelter treatment/refining charges, and secular demand growth from electrification, grid build-out, AI data centers and the broader energy transition. Zinc is in modest surplus (an estimated 40,000t surplus in 2025, 63,000t forecast for 2026) with mine supply growth outpacing still-sluggish demand, particularly in North America and China.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — Teck is a classic cyclical commodity producer; revenue, margins and cash flow move directly with LME copper and zinc prices and global industrial demand
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct balance-sheet sensitivity (Teck is now net-cash with falling debt), but moderate indirect sensitivity via the effect of global growth/rate expectations on industrial metals demand and investment in capital-intensive growth projects
key_input_costs: Labour (unionized workforces at QB2, HVC, Red Dog, Trail)
Steel/construction materials for HVC MLE and QB2 TMF capex programs

recent_developments.event: Teck and Anglo American plc announced a merger of equals to form Anglo Teck plc, a Canada-headquartered top-five global copper producer, expected to close within 12-18 months of announcement

Shareholders of both Teck and Anglo American approved the merger (Dec 9); Government of Canada approved the merger under the Investment Canada Act with binding Canadian investment commitments (Dec 15)
Teck disclosed a QB shiploader outage repair completion timeline and updated Antamina 2026 zinc guidance to 35,000-45,000 tonnes

FY2025 annual results: adjusted EBITDA of C$4.3bn, profit from continuing operations attributable to shareholders of C$1.4bn (C$2.84/share); net cash position; US$1.3bn returned to shareholders via buybacks and dividends in 2025; HVC MLE sanctioned mid-2025 (life extended to 2046)

Q2 2026 results: adjusted EBITDA of C$2.2bn, up 204% YoY, on record copper prices (US$6.05/lb average) and a third consecutive quarter of stable QB2 production; copper production up 25% YoY to 135,900 tonnes; net cash position increased by C$756m in the quarter; liquidity of C$10.3bn

Strategic Investment Agreement signed with Canada Growth Fund and Natural Resources Canada's Critical Minerals Accelerator to expand germanium, gallium and antimony production capacity at Trail Operations
Bondholder consent secured for note amendments tied to the Anglo American merger structure
Teck and Anglo American extended the special dividend payment timeline associated with the merger; Executive Leadership Team for the combined Anglo Teck announced

Teck scheduled to report Q3 2026 results on October 29, 2026 (after this analysis date); merger remains pending final international regulatory approvals (China, South Korea decisions outstanding as of mid-2026)

items.notes: Unchanged from previously disclosed guidance; compares to 453,500 tonnes produced in 2025
Declining from 565,000 tonnes in 2025 as Red Dog grades decline; Antamina zinc guidance updated to 35,000-45,000 tonnes (Teck's 22.5% share) reflecting a finalized mine plan
Compares to 229,900 tonnes produced in 2025 at Trail Operations

items.metric: QB copper net cash unit costs
items.notes: Improvement from 2025 actual of US$2.67/lb, driven by higher production, higher molybdenum by-product credits, and shiploader return to service

items.metric: Total copper net cash unit costs (company-wide, incl. QB)
items.notes: In line with 2025 net cash unit costs of US$2.03/lb
Higher than 2025's US$0.33/lb due to lower production/grades expected, mostly at Red Dog
Includes C$390-460m for QB TMF development work
Includes C$900m-1.2bn for HVC MLE; remainder for Zafranal/other near-term copper growth engineering and permitting
Growth driven by QB ramp maturity and HVC MLE; 2028 QB grades expected to dip before improving
Structural decline as Red Dog nears end of mine life absent a sanctioned mine-life extension

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jonathan Price has framed 2025-2026 results as validating the 'copper-focused strategy,' citing QB's third consecutive quarter of stable operations in Q2 2026 as evidence the ramp-up is maturing, and has positioned the pending Anglo American merger as the 'next evolution' of Teck's transformation from a diversified coal/copper/zinc miner into a pure-play critical minerals company. Management has reiterated the Anglo Teck merger is expected to close within the original 12-18 month window from the September 2025 announcement (i.e., by roughly March 2027), pending remaining international regulatory approvals. Management has also signaled a pause in sanctioning further copper growth projects beyond HVC MLE (Zafranal, San Nicolás) to prioritize QB2 execution, per the Comprehensive Operational Review completed in 2025.

bull_case: QB2 ramp-up is inflecting positively — three consecutive quarters of stable production and falling unit costs through mid-2026 suggest the asset is finally converting from a cash drag into a major cash generator, with further upside as the TMF sand wedge completes in 2026 and grades improve post-2028

Record/strong copper prices (LME averaged over $6/lb in Q2 2026) combined with rising copper volumes are driving outsized earnings growth (adjusted EBITDA +204% YoY in Q2 2026), and Teck has high operating leverage to further copper price strength from AI/data-center and grid electrification demand

Pending Anglo American merger would create Anglo Teck, a top-five global copper producer with ~US$800m/year of run-rate synergies and a long-dated option on US$1.4bn/year of EBITDA uplift from integrating QB2 with Anglo's adjacent Collahuasi mine — a scale and portfolio-quality upgrade for current shareholders

Strong balance sheet (net cash position, C$9-10bn+ of liquidity) gives Teck/Anglo Teck flexibility to fund the copper growth pipeline (HVC MLE, Zafranal, San Nicolás) and continue capital returns without needing to raise capital through a commodity downturn

Successful, disciplined divestiture of the coal business at an attractive valuation (US$8.6bn total EVR proceeds) demonstrates management credibility in capital allocation and portfolio simplification
bear_case: Merger completion risk is real and prolonged — the Anglo Teck deal still awaits international regulatory approvals (China, South Korea) as of mid-2026, faces Canadian political/investor pushback over deal terms and the 'zero premium' framing, and a long approval window leaves room for delay, renegotiation, or a rival bid

QB2 has a troubled execution history (TMF tailings constraints across 2023-2025, a 2025 port shiploader outage) and even with recent stabilization, the asset has not yet operated at design throughput/recoveries for a sustained multi-year period — execution risk is not fully retired

Zinc segment is in structural decline as Red Dog approaches end of mine life, removing a formerly stable cash-flow contributor unless a mine-life extension is sanctioned; this leaves Teck increasingly dependent on copper price cycles for earnings

Commodity-price dependency cuts both ways — FY2024 continuing operations posted a pre-tax loss, illustrating how quickly results can turn negative if copper/zinc prices retreat from current elevated levels, especially given still-maturing cost structure at QB2

QB2 partner advances (~US$3.1bn from Sumitomo) sit outside headline 'total debt' figures, meaning standard leverage ratios understate total balance-sheet claims ahead of common equity; investors comparing Teck's leverage to peers on reported debt alone may be overstating balance-sheet strength
